articleTitle: DLTFS Study of Monolithically Integrated GaN-on-Si Power Transistor for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: This paper deals with the defect study of a monolithically integrated GaN power transistor on a conductive Si substrate by Deep Level Transient Fourier Spectroscopy method (DLTFS). Due to the high non-exponentiality of measured capacitance transients we focused only on defects that were determined with high certainty in the investigated samples and confirmed by measurements under different conditions. Parameters of six electrically active defects with activation energies 0.28, 0.53, 0.81, 0.92, 0.09 a 0.84 eV were determined. The origin of these defects probably corresponds to dislocation extended from the GaN separating layer to the AlGaN layer, nitrogen point defects (vacancies and interstitials) or dislocations. We observed that the signal significantly increases in the low-temperature range at positive reverse voltages.

articleTitle: The Influence of a Substrate Heating on the Contact Resistance of DNTT Organic Field-Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this contribution, we deal with the optimization of fabrication process of the organic field-effect transistor (OFET) devices with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> dielectric, using the DNTT organic semiconductor. Especially, the influence of a substrate heating on the electrical properties, with the greatest emphasis on charge carrier mobility in saturated region (μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) and contact resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>). Activation energy according to the thermodynamic laws of the Arrhenius plot was estimated to 284 meV. This effect is linked to favoring the more inclined growth of triclinic molecular structures, improving the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) overlap, and/or increasing the specific surface area. A slight increase in μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> also correlated with the higher fabrication temperature. These findings provide insight into optimizing the OFETs electrical performance.

articleTitle: Power density improvements for electronic fuse (eFuse)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: Goal of the paper is to evaluate the power density increase options for single channel integrated eFuse device with focus on pass device, comparing different MOSFET solutions using Si and Wide Bandgap materials also adding system voltage rail level consideration to maximize the power delivered to the load while keeping the pass semiconductor device area constant. The resulting power enhanced final solution size is the same.TRIZ inventive methodology was applied.

articleTitle: Influence of InAlN layer Mg doping on the quality of InN/In0.61Al0.39N heterostructure deposited by MOCVD
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.61</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.39</inf>N layers were doped by Mg using a variable flow of the Cp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mg precursor at 30 or 80 nmol/min to serve as buffer layers for thin InN layer growth on sapphire substrates by MOCVD. XRD, TEM, SEM, and AFM analyses showed a deterioration of the InAlN structural quality together with phase separation on a nanometer scale with a notable In/Al composition modulation towards the surface of the InAlN layer for the higher Cp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mg flow. The extracted InN electron mobility also decreased from 471 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs for the Cp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mg flow of 30 nmol/min to 380 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs for the Cp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Mg flow of 80 nmol/min.

articleTitle: 3D polymer probes and cantilevers with various geometry for application in AFM
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) enables high-resolution imaging of a sample surface based on atomic interactions between the surface and a scanning probe. Geometry, and material composition of fiber tip and cantilever strongly influence the capability of any measurement and can be tailored to the desired application. There are two typical geometries used for AFM cantilevers: V-shaped and simple rectangular geometry. We focused on design and fabrication of novel probes based on polymer with different cantilevers. We investigate both type of cantilevers V-shaped and rectangular. Also, different tips based on polymer were proposed and fabricated. The final probes were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and their quality was analysed by scanning the AFM images.

articleTitle: Impact of Indium Content on Defect Distribution in InGaN/GaN QW Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a Deep-Level Transient Fourier Spectroscopy (DLTFS) study on emission processes in InGaN/GaN quantum well (QW) structures with 15% and 23% indium content. Emission from the QW was confirmed with an activation energy of 0.08 eV for the structure with 15% indium and 0.12 eV for the structure with 23% indium. Several hole traps were identified, likely associated with nitrogen and gallium point defects, as well as defect clusters along screw- and mixed-type dislocations. Interestingly, a lower-than-expected trap concentration was observed in the structure with higher indium content. We assume this is caused by emissions from dislocations, which represent electron trap. The observed DLTFS signal is the combination of these emissions.

articleTitle: Quality-Based ECG Classification: Deep Learning Approach for Long-Duration Holter Recordings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this contribution, we propose a deep learning-based method for automatically segmenting and classifying electrocardiogtam (ECG) signal quality from extended Holter recordings. Without relying on accelerometer data, we developed a custom dataset of 187,000 samples, where ECG signals were split into small segments and manually labeled for quality. A convolutional-recurrent neural network was trained to differentiate usable ECG segments, achieving an F1 score of 90.06 %. This automated approach streamlines the processing of long-duration Holter data, allowing clinicians to focus on high-quality, clinically relevant information.

articleTitle: Enhancing of the GaN HEMTs Devices through Advanced Innovative Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: The widespread adoption of the wide bandgap AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) is limited mainly due to their higher cost compared to silicon devices. Even so, for power conversion and RF applications, AlGaN/GaN HEMTs offer a better alternative to silicon device. This article described fabricated innovative AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on Si based on Asymmetric waffle, Square waffle and Octagon waffle gate patterns which refer to conventional Finger structures. We have analyzed the topologies in terms of specific resistance reduction that can lead to area savings and thus cost reduction. The 2D simulation and DC Measurements of involved devices confirm the suppression of the specific resistance for Asymmetric waffle, Square waffle and Octagon waffle gate patterns, by 36%, 40% and 43% respectively, comparing to the Finger topology.

articleTitle: Short-term memory in organic field-effect transistor at cryogenic temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In the last few years an emphasis has been placed on the increase computing capabilities of computer processors. Nearly all modern computers are based on the von Neuman architecture. The operation of the von Neuman architecture requires a vast amount of data transmission between the separated computation core/processor and the memory unit, executing instructions in sequence. Now that we enter the age of artificial intelligence which will for the foreseeable future require more complex and power demanding hardware, requiring alternative architectures. This compelled researchers to look at the function of the human brain for inspiration. The brain processes information in parallel across a vast network of interconnected neurons. This allows for much faster and more efficient information processing, furthermore, it operates remarkably efficiently with low energy consumption, with a degree of fault tolerance. The principle of neuromorphic computing is based on an electric device which can mimic biological synapses. A synapse is the communication junction between neurons. Organic materials are explored for the use as artificial synapses due to their properties compared to standard semiconductors. This study explores the use as artificial synapses based on OFETs and its memory effect. The devices were fabricated using a bottom-gate top-contact geometry, exhibit a significant short-term memory effect at cryogenic temperatures (200 K), characterized by a maximum current gain under of 9.27 µA after 25 optical pulses. Two distinct relaxation times, τ₁ = 0.055 ± 0.001 s and τ₂ = 1.036 ± 0.012 s, indicate the presence of multiple trap states.

articleTitle: OCT for biophotonics applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this work, we present the establishment of an OCT workplace and the analysis of samples made from combinate of two materials. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and photoresist (AZ5214E) were chosen due to their similarity to biological samples in terms of refractive index and absorption, enabling realistic simulations and testing. At the OCT workstation, we conducted a detailed analysis of these samples, focusing on obtaining high-quality 3D intensity maps, which are crucial for biophotonics applications.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Element for Biomedical Use
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: The article deals with the properties of a piezoelectric generator primarily intended as a piezoelectric breathing sensor for use in medicine. Mechanical frequencies are usually in units of Hz. The content of the article belongs to the category of renewable energy sources with the conversion of environmental energy into electrical energy with a focus on use in biomedicine. The aim of the future is to further hybrid integration. A piezoelectric element "sleep monitor strip 10184000-01" was used to implement the feature analysis.

articleTitle: Polymer Elements for Lab-on-Fiber – A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this paper, we present an overview of the prepared polymer elements for lab-on-fiber (LOF) developed at the University of Zilina. In recent years, lab-on-fiber has become a highly popular topic. This technique integrates the well-known properties of optical fibers with innovative polymer structure fabrication methods. The structures are created using modern 3D laser printing. With our sensors, it was possible to measure quantities such as temperature, pressure, change in refractive index, or the concentration of organic compounds such as isopropanol, acetone, toluene, and chloroform.

articleTitle: Preliminary Evaluation of PBTI and Back-Effect interplay in 100 V p-GaN gate AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this paper, we aim to analyse the behaviour of 100 V p-GaN gate AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under varying measurement conditions, focusing on the interplay between Positive Bias Temperature Instability (PBTI) and the Back-Effect (BE). Two stress sequences have been performed to underline the impact of the hole injection due to the gate voltage, the electrostatic coupling and the negatively ionized buffer traps caused by the substrate voltage, which emulates the application conditions of the high-side device in half-bridge topology. Different behaviours have been observed among the two tests, highlighting in both cases the recovery of the drain current during the stress thanks to relatively high gate potential. This approach allows us to clearly discern the PBTI and BE contributions to the dynamic behaviour of the device under test.

articleTitle: Design of Packaging of Power DMOS Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: A simulation study of the packaging of a power double-diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (DMOS) transistor is presented. The investigation focuses on refining the design to enhance the device's electrical performance. The simulation findings show that an optimized design can improve the switching speed of the power DMOS transistor. The ribbon-bond source electrode's reduced parasitic inductance and resistance enhance the switching speed of the power DMOS transistor by around 13%.

articleTitle: Combining laser interference lithography and direct write lithography for hierarchical structures fabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this contribution, we focus on the fabrication of hierarchical structures by combining two lithography techniques. Direct write lithography (DWL) is used to achieve arbitrary surface profiles. The second level structure is reached by applying laser interference lithography (LIL). Specifically, the saw-tooth grating was designed as a large-scale element, additionally patterned with a sub-micron LIL structure. The experimental work demonstrated that integrating these two technologies allows effective fabrication of hierarchical structures. The sample was initially patterned using DWL to form saw-tooth structure having a 100 μm period. Subsequently, a 0.69 μm periodic structure was added using LIL. To examine the quality of the grating, confocal microscopy and scanning electron microscopy was used.

articleTitle: NSOM characterization of polymer table-like mirror grating prepared by laser lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: In this paper, we focused on a specific concept of the grating with the table-like arrangement. We prepared the grating structure in IP-Dip material using three-dimensional (3D) laser lithography according to the proposed theoretical design. The morphology of the prepared structures was analyzed using a confocal microscope and scanning electron microscope. Finally, we experimentally demonstrated highly resolved near-field scanning optical microscope (NSOM) for the optical near field distribution in transmission mode over the table-like grating mirror structure.

articleTitle: Using Symbolic Regression Metamodels for Integrated Circuits Production
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: The paper introduces a Machine Learning QLattice metamodel that can be used as a more efficient substitute for the circuit simulators in the integrated circuit industry with less compute effort. QLattice represents a Symbolic Regression metamodel that is based on Genetic Programming. The purpose of this metamodel is to find the best mathematical formula that achieves the optimal correlation between the inputs and the output. We made a comparative analysis between two regression metamodels, namely QLattice and Gaussian Process, on synthetic functions that emulate real circuits behaviour, as well as on the datasets used for real-life product development.

articleTitle: Electron mobility analysis of InN/In0.61Al0.39N heterostructure after HCl treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of structural and charge transport properties of high-quality N-polar InN/In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.61</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.39</inf>N heterostructures grown by metalorganic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD). We observed a strong correlation between the HCl surface treatment and electron mobility. The mobility reduction for structure without AlN nucleation was affected by a thinner native surface oxide formation (supported by the lower I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> area ratio ~ 0.7), where the surface roughness could play a more significant role.

articleTitle: Neural Network for Calibration of Electrical Models of Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a neural network-based approach for the calibration of electrical models of semiconductor devices, focusing on diodes and MOSFET transistors. Extensive datasets from experimental measurements and simulations were utilized to train and validate the models. The calibrated models demonstrated high accuracy and performance across diverse operational conditions, proving the effectiveness of neural networks in automating the calibration process. This research advances the field of semiconductor modelling, with significant potential for application in optimizing device performance.

articleTitle: Design of Power SiC Transistor Embedded in PCB Supported by 3D Thermo-Mechanical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: This study presents a thermo-mechanical simulation of a power SiC transistor integrated into a printed circuit board (PCB). The primary objective is to optimize the design to enhance the thermal and mechanical properties of the device. Through numerical simulations, critical areas within systems utilizing power transistors embedded in PCBs are identified and optimized to reduce mechanical strain and improve heat dissipation. These improvements contribute to the overall reliability of the final system.

articleTitle: Simple RF on-chip calibration for high-frequency transistor measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Advanced Semiconductor Devices and Microsystems (ASDAM)
abstract: The field of high-frequency device research requires the utilization of a vector network analyser and the advanced calibration methods to correct measurement imperfections caused by two RF signal paths, from the signal generator/detector to the probe tips and probe tips to the on-chip device under test (DUT). Plenty of the calibration methods utilizing reference RF devices including robust calculations were already introduced. This paper deals with imperfection correction of the probe tips to the on-chip DUT RF signal path. OPEN, SHORT, THRU on-chip test structures are used together with iteration calculations which allow for a simple implementation into automated calibration process. Vector error correction of s- parameters obtained by calibration process are subsequently employed in de- embedding process to acquire s-parameters of a DUT.
